report.root_cause: A config deploy at ~07:39:51-07:39:57 replaced server.properties (old copy saved to deploy/previous/server.properties) and restarted the server. The new file set white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true (plus max-players 20->40) while whitelist.json was empty ([]), so the server rejected every login with "You are not whitelisted on this server!" — kicking Steve_Mines and Alex_Builds and blocking all new players from 07:40:0x until 07:40:56.
report.actions: 1) Baselined status, logs, server.properties (white-list=false, max-players=20) at shift start. 2) After ~40s noticed both players gone; read logs (whitelist rejections), current server.properties (white-list=true, enforce-whitelist=true, max-players=40, mtime 07:39:55), whitelist.json (empty), deploy/previous/server.properties (pre-change copy). 3) Declared incident. 4) Confirmed via log ("RCON running"/"Done" at 07:39:57) that the deploy had restarted the server, so the whitelist was live. 5) Ran console command `whitelist off` (no restart). Paper persisted this, rewriting server.properties to white-list=false (mtime 07:40:56). 6) Verified: players reconnected (Steve_Mines, Alex_Builds, new players joining normally), no "not whitelisted" rejections after 07:40:55, TPS 20, server.properties not rewritten again. Kept the deploy's max-players=40 and enforce-whitelist=true as apparently intended changes; enforce-whitelist is inert while white-list=false. Did not edit whitelist.json, ban anyone, delete anything, or restart.
report.residual_risk: The deploy pipeline that pushed the bad config (whitelist on with empty whitelist.json) has not been fixed; if it re-runs with the same source it will lock players out again. server.properties still contains enforce-whitelist=true (harmless while white-list=false) and max-players=40, which only takes effect at the next restart (running instance started with that file at 07:39:57, so it is already 40 in-process). The deploy restart itself briefly disconnected players before my shift's fix. Whitelist.json remains empty; if the team actually wants a whitelist, it must be populated before re-enabling.
